newsitem.title: USA: Wells-Gardner sees improved '97 second half.
newsitem.headline: Wells-Gardner sees improved '97 second half.

text.p: Wells-Gardner Electronics Corp said Tuesday it is "confident" that results in the second half of 1997 will improve upon last year's second half performance of sales of $17.1 million and a net loss of $13,000.
The monitor manufacturer also said margins increased to 17.7 percent in the second quarter of 1997 from 13.3 in the first quarter, 1997.
The increase was due to a combination of improved productivity, a royalty adjustment of $112,000 and the elimination of low margin products, the company said.
Wells-Gardner plans to release 13 new products in 1997, several of which are part of the program to increase margins by both reducing cost and adding features to the products, the company said.
Earlier Tuesday, the company reported second quarter net income of $448,000, or $0.11 a share, compared to $151,000, or $0.04 a share, a year ago.

"The sales growth was driven by gains in service, bartop, gaming, automotive and kiosk monitor sales," chief executive officer Anthony Spier said in a news release. "The earnings improvement was driven by increased sales volume and higher margins."
